collision_disclosure: families sharing a property vector cannot be distinguished by this benchmark. Any such pair is reported as a limitation of the vector and BOTH are scored as unresolved, rather than crediting a recovery to whichever family is convenient.

K4-A01.kill_condition: a cheaper admissible parent exists at the predicted crossover
K4-A01.negative_twin: replace the shared affine law with independent per-input labels
K4-A01.phase_prediction: wins when the target is an affine function of the inputs and reuse is high; loses to memory when the input set is small enough to enumerate

K4-A02.kill_condition: an explicit finite feature map dominates at matched risk
K4-A02.phase_prediction: wins when the target is smooth in a fixed similarity and the sample is small; loses when an explicit small feature map suffices

K4-A03.kill_condition: an unpriced index, or aliasing across records
K4-A03.negative_twin: values generated by a stable low-dimensional law with high reuse
K4-A03.phase_prediction: wins when records are independent and volatile; loses when a low-dimensional law generates them

K4-A04.kill_condition: posterior aliasing under a separating utility
K4-A04.phase_prediction: wins when the utility is uncertainty-sensitive and evidence is ambiguous; loses under a restricted loss where a point estimate suffices

K4-A05.kill_condition: an approximate parent is admissible at the same theta
K4-A05.negative_twin: constraints relaxed to a smooth objective
K4-A05.phase_prediction: wins when constraints are exact and the answer must be certified; loses when an approximate response is admissible

K4-A06.kill_condition: an admissible compiled parent is cheaper at H=1
K4-A06.negative_twin: remove the verifier so candidates cannot be checked
K4-A06.phase_prediction: wins at low reuse where compiling is not amortized; loses at high reuse to a compiled table

K4-A07.kill_condition: a stateless parent matches at the same theta
K4-A07.negative_twin: shuffle the sequence so order carries no information
K4-A07.phase_prediction: wins when the dependence is long-range and the state is small; loses to full-context comparison when length is short

K4-A08.kill_condition: a nonlinear recurrent parent is required for admissibility
K4-A08.negative_twin: make the dynamics input-dependent and nonlinear
K4-A08.phase_prediction: wins when the dynamics are linear-time-invariant and length is large

K4-A09.kill_condition: an unshared parent is not more expensive at matched risk
K4-A09.negative_twin: break the equivariance by making the answer position-dependent
K4-A09.phase_prediction: wins when the target commutes with the declared shift group; loses when position matters

K4-A10.negative_twin: randomize the edge set so adjacency carries no information
K4-A10.phase_prediction: wins when the answer depends on graph neighbourhoods; loses when the graph is complete or empty

K4-A11.kill_condition: a fixed-routing parent matches at the same theta
K4-A11.negative_twin: fix the mixing pattern so it cannot depend on content
K4-A11.phase_prediction: wins when which inputs matter depends on the input itself; loses to fixed routing when the dependence is static

K4-A12.kill_condition: dense mixing is cheaper at the predicted window fraction
K4-A12.negative_twin: make the required dependence dense and long-range
K4-A12.phase_prediction: wins when the content dependence is local or low-rank; the crossover against dense mixing is at the declared window fraction

K4-A13.kill_condition: a dense parent matches at matched quality and lower total burden
K4-A13.negative_twin: make the modes fully overlapping so no partition helps
K4-A13.phase_prediction: wins when modes are separable and the router is accurate; loses to a dense parent when modes overlap

K4-A14.kill_condition: an internalized parent is admissible and cheaper
K4-A14.negative_twin: make every fact stable and small enough to internalize
K4-A14.phase_prediction: wins when facts are volatile and must be attributable; loses when facts are stable and few

K4-A15.kill_condition: a full update is cheaper at the predicted rank
K4-A15.phase_prediction: wins when the revision is low-rank relative to the core; loses when it is full-rank

K4-A16.kill_condition: a single member matches at the same risk
K4-A16.negative_twin: make all members identical so averaging buys nothing
K4-A16.phase_prediction: wins when member errors are weakly correlated; loses when they are correlated

K4-A17.kill_condition: an unverified parent is admissible at the same theta
K4-A17.negative_twin: make verification as expensive as proposing
K4-A17.phase_prediction: wins when checking is much cheaper than proposing and proposals are unreliable

K4-A18.kill_condition: a direct policy parent is cheaper across the goal distribution
K4-A18.negative_twin: a single fixed goal for the whole lifetime
K4-A18.phase_prediction: wins when dynamics are reused across many goals; loses at a single fixed goal

K4-A19.kill_condition: a model-based parent is cheaper across the goal distribution
K4-A19.negative_twin: make the goal change every episode
K4-A19.phase_prediction: wins at a fixed goal with cheap interaction; loses when goals change and dynamics are reusable

K4-A20.kill_condition: a non-sequential parent matches at lower total burden
K4-A20.negative_twin: require a jointly consistent answer with no admissible order
K4-A20.phase_prediction: wins when the factorization order is natural and latency is per-token; loses when global coherence dominates

K4-A21.kill_condition: a sequential parent matches at fewer total charged steps
K4-A21.negative_twin: reduce the target to one dimension
K4-A21.phase_prediction: wins when the target is high-dimensional and jointly constrained; the crossover against sequential is at the declared step count

K4-A22.kill_condition: a full-dimensional parent matches at the same quality
K4-A22.negative_twin: make the data full-dimensional with no manifold structure
K4-A22.phase_prediction: wins when the data lie near a low-dimensional manifold; loses when they do not

grammar_independence_note: three grammars with disjoint primitive sets and disjoint state models. Reminting one grammar does not count as independence and is not done here. NOTE under IG-5: all three are authored by the same process, so agreement between them rules out implementation artifacts but NOT shared conceptual bias about which primitives are natural. That residue is open and is not claimed closed.

grammars.G1_TENSOR_GRAPH: typed dataflow over finite-width numeric buffers: elementwise arithmetic, reduction, indexed gather/scatter, comparison, branch, bounded iteration, explicit random-bit draw. No convolution, attention, gate, expert, retriever or adapter macro.
grammars.G2_SYMBOLIC_PROGRAM: register machine over scalars and arrays: load/store, arithmetic, comparison, conditional jump, bounded loop, explicit random-bit draw, callable sub-programs. No architecture macro.
grammars.G3_FSM_MESSAGE: finite-state automata with typed message passing on a declared topology: local transition tables, send/receive, bounded rounds, explicit random-bit draw. No architecture macro.

independence_status.IG-1_generator: CLOSED_BY_EXHAUSTION where the obligation class is a complete enumeration at the declared cap; otherwise IG-2 applies
independence_status.IG-2_seed: CLOSED_BY_FUTURE_ENTROPY -- seed rule committed here, resolved against a public value that does not exist yet
independence_status.IG-3_leakage: CLOSED_BY_WITNESSED_COMMIT -- this freeze is pushed to GitHub before any result exists

controls: CTL_LOOKUP: recall 4 taught key-value pairs exactly
CTL_AFFINE: an affine function of 4 inputs with coefficients on the declared grid
known_control_recovery.coverage_bound: a cell is search-limited only if scored candidates >= 1e6 OR the expressible set at the declared caps was exhausted; both are recorded per cell.
known_control_recovery.purpose: preregistered known-control recovery. INCONCLUSIVE_SEARCH may be claimed ONLY if every control below is recovered by the same grammar, budget and seed policy in the same cell. If a control fails, the cell is INCONCLUSIVE_GRAMMAR or a harness fault -- never INCONCLUSIVE_SEARCH, and never THEORY_RED.

name_key_warning: name_key is for human adjudication AFTER scoring. The runner must not read it. A name leak invalidates the zero-prior evidence.
purpose: leave-one-family-out neutral rediscovery; prediction frozen BEFORE any search

verdicts.INCONCLUSIVE_GRAMMAR: held-out semantics not expressible in this grammar at the declared caps
verdicts.INCONCLUSIVE_SEARCH: expressible, budget exhausted, AND every known control recovered in the same cell
verdicts.K4_RECOVERY_GREEN: admissible machine found by name-blind search whose MEASURED property vector equals the frozen predicted vector for the held-out family
verdicts.THEORY_RED: admissible machine found whose measured vector CONTRADICTS the frozen prediction
